workflow.title: Choose evidence before changing restaurant staffing
workflow.question: What is a question worth before changing restaurant staffing?
workflow.description: Compare choosing staffing now with a records audit or a complete four-dinner trial. Import all study-and-response operating constraints, charge each full evidence price once, and value noisy report responses over the stated future dinner horizon. Audit an optional actual report before reconsidering the remaining dinners from its original conditional probabilities.

Module authors supply these declarations and domain vocabulary. Case workers supply only values allowed by the frozen module. Facts, scenarios and operating permission must never be inferred from a preferred plan.

definition.title: Complete a commitment
definition.responsibility: Find one complete static operating choice that satisfies every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted joint scenario, then compare feasible choices.
invariants: Choices are finite, input-only controls. One complete assignment is shared across every admitted scenario and obligation.
Admitted joint scenarios are explicit facts; neither independence, probabilities nor unlisted scenarios are inferred.
An empty admitted basis is inconsistent, never a vacuous feasibility result.
Typed acyclic expressions separate static controls, scenario consequences and post-scenario preference aggregates.
Activities, calendars, bookings and permission validity use half-open intervals; adjacent intervals do not overlap.
Capacity is the sum of simultaneous renewable demands. A scoped grant must cover its entire required operation.
Expense sums nonrefundable charges. Refundable holds affect cash only; simultaneous cash events are netted before peak cash is measured.
Every mandatory condition must pass for the same choice in every admitted scenario. Preference cannot compensate for failure.
Ranking is lexicographic over feasible choices only; genuine ties are retained and identifiers only stabilize display order.
A fully checked witness establishes existence during partial search. No-plan and optimality claims require complete relevant coverage.
Missing data, unresolved lookups, unsafe arithmetic and unsupported declarations are invalid input, never invented facts.
Calculated feasibility is conditional on accepted facts and fixed assumptions, not permission, reservation or evidence of actual completion.

expressionLanguage.literals: Finite scalar or homogeneous scalar-array data; no executable code.

operators.add: At least two compatible numbers -> number
operators.mul: Two numbers with at most one dimensional operand -> number; count is a multiplicity
operators.lookup: Complete primary-key binding in a typed input table -> exactly one selected scalar; missing or ambiguous lookup is invalid
operators.exists: Typed equality bindings plus optional row-scoped predicate -> boolean; no match is false
operators.interval-covered: Typed selected calendar rows and a positive half-open interval -> boolean; adjacent coverage may combine
operators.worst-case: Numeric expression -> maximum across admitted scenarios for preference only; nested or unreduced scenario aggregates are invalid

caseDerivation: All case parameters and keyed input rows use the frozen module.inputs types, units, bounds, keys and references; no missing-value defaults or coercion are inferred.
Finite choices draw only from input arrays, input table columns or fixed literal domains; the same assignment applies to every scenario.
The scenarioDomain table explicitly lists admitted joint scenarios; an empty table is an inconsistent basis rather than vacuous feasibility.
Activity graphs, constraints, mandatory obligations, resource mappings, financial mode and preference remain frozen module declarations.
Provenance describes accepted factual sources; identifying a source does not authenticate it or infer readiness.

module.title: Complete a restaurant staffing test and response
module.question: Can this complete learning option and later staffing response operate within the declared time, people and spending limits?
module.description: Compare six complete learning-and-response plans across both admitted outcomes before comparing the value of information.
assumptions: The four fixed dinner starts are November 13, 20, 27 and December 4, 2026 at 18:00. The declared serviceHours applies to all four; the three-hour example ends at 21:00.
A trial observes every dinner and hires the extra runner for November 20 and December 4. Observation is continuous work requiring a separate person while the host station remains covered.

Unassigned allocation resources are inactive placeholders for contexts that do not conduct the trial. They have zero payroll and never use an operating person. Every real activity resource demand is one whole person.
The trial price is derived from the same four observation allocations and two runner allocations, their shared serviceHours and the accepted hourly rates. No independent trial quote is substituted.
The audit is a complete accepted flat fee. The budget is authority to spend on learning; it is not available cash and does not fund hypothetical future wages.

The per-dinner upside and downside are incremental NET monetary outcomes for the future runner setup, already including future runner wages. Usual staffing has zero incremental payoff. Learning fees are separate and counted once.

November 13 at noon as the starting time, a two-hour audit, December 5 at 21:00 as trial answer time and December 7 at noon as the decision deadline are explicit additional fictional timing premises, not dates claimed from the source document.

When an actual report arrives, reassess only future choices with currentTime equal to its actual receipt time and futureDinnerCount equal to the remaining horizon. The no-study context does not recharge a sunk study fee.

Every choice is checked under both admitted outcomes. A probability or favorable report never waives the operational conditions. This assessment does not hire anyone, purchase a study or publish a roster.

requirements.label: Keep the complete declared basis
requirements.meaning: The supplied helper rows retain their authored identities, exclusive capacities and exact zero-or-one cost factors. Both possible staffing outcomes remain admitted.

requirements.label: Complete accepted study prices
requirements.meaning: Every selected paid learning option has a complete accepted price covering all of its declared work.

requirements.label: Accepted learning spending limit
requirements.meaning: The complete selected study fee fits the accepted learning budget. This is a spending limit, not a forecast of cash receipts.

requirements.label: Learning can finish before the choice
requirements.meaning: A new trial starts before its first fixed dinner, includes all four observations, and supplies its answer before the decision deadline. A selected audit also finishes by that deadline.

requirements.label: Separate people for concurrent work
requirements.meaning: The host keeps the host station covered. One person cannot cover that station and conduct simultaneous observation; paid trial runner work also needs an available runner.

requirements.label: A timely available future staffing response
requirements.meaning: A newly chosen future runner commitment must be made by the decision deadline with the runner available. The usual setup remains a complete fallback.

module.title: Review a received staffing signal
module.description: Establish the identity and usability of an actual audit or trial report from its supplied receipt, design, scope and observation records.
module.question: Is this received report a usable signal for the declared staffing decision?
module.boundary: One declared runner role, dinner peak service window, set of observed study services, observation dates and signal-design version. The study-service count is separate from the number of future comparable dinners used for valuation. Audit and trial reports are imperfect signals. This module establishes receipt identity and scope only; it does not estimate a staffing effect, infer probabilities, or establish whether adding staff improves contribution.

assumptions: Accepted receipt records accurately describe the supplied report and its provenance. This evaluation does not authenticate the underlying physical records.
Audit and trial are distinct study identities. Favorable, unfavorable and unusable describe the received signal, not the true operating effect.

Usability requires the published scope identifier, design and version, role, service window and dates to match the declared scope exactly, with complete records and identified sources. Future comparable dinners belong to the valuation and do not change this report scope.

The trial requires four declared study services and full observation coverage. The records audit creates no prospective study services. At least one audit record is an explicit minimum record-presence premise, not a claim of statistical sufficiency or causal accuracy.
An omitted qualification record leaves usability open. Explicitly conflicting accepted records remain inconsistent; neither missing records nor explanation counts supply probabilities.

questions.label: Future dinners

questions.meaning: The accepted complete hourly expense in USD cents. Observation covers all four authored dinners.

questions.label: Complete three-hour dinner service

questions.label: Use the working host as observer

questions.label: Trial price complete

questions.label: Audit price complete

questions.meaning: A partial quote cannot establish the full purchase expense.

questions.label: Complete audit fee

questions.label: Study purchase authority

questions.meaning: A study purchase limit in USD cents. This is not a cash balance for future restaurant operations.

questions.label: Current decision time

questions.label: Staffing decision cutoff

questions.meaning: The usable answer and the future runner decision must arrive by this elapsed-minute cutoff.

questions.label: Audit turnaround
questions.question: How long until the audit supplies an answer?
questions.meaning: Elapsed minutes from purchase to a usable audit answer.

questions.label: Trial answer time
questions.question: When will the four-dinner trial supply its answer?
questions.meaning: The absolute elapsed minute when the complete trial report is available.

questions.label: Future runner availability
questions.question: Can the runner cover the future dinners?
questions.meaning: A favorable report never supplies absent operating capacity.

questions.label: Runner net upside per dinner
questions.question: What net contribution would a runner add when the change is worthwhile?
questions.meaning: Net incremental contribution after future runner wages. The complete future payoff is this amount multiplied by the number of future dinners.

questions.label: Runner net downside per dinner

questions.label: Other staff commitments

questions.meaning: Complete recorded outside commitments remain part of every study-and-response operating check.

questions.label: Prior staffing probabilities

questions.label: Audit and trial report likelihoods

questions.label: Optional actual report and remaining horizon

questions.meaning: Optional received records and remaining operating horizon. Receipt alone never establishes the staffing situation or authorizes a staffing change.

sections.title: Complete study and response operating findings

value.scope: A runner staffing choice, one evidence purchase at most, four authored study services, and a separate stated number of future comparable dinners.
assumptions: The future runner payoffs are net per-dinner contributions after future wages; the operating app scales them automatically by the future dinner count.
The paid trial includes the runner on two complete services and an observer on all four. The complete native study fee is charged once by the learning comparison.
The study purchase limit is purchase authority, not an operating cash balance.
Both staffing situations remain logically possible after every report. Zero prior or report weights never waive the study-and-response operating requirements.
Reports have declared conditional likelihoods. A favorable answer is noisy evidence and is not an accepted fact that the runner is worthwhile.
Retain the current roster when expected staffing values tie. This tie policy is separate from the value calculation.
After receipt, use the original matching possible branch posterior, the actual receipt time and the remaining dinner count. Previously paid evidence expense is sunk and is not charged again.

sheets.meaning: Net incremental contribution after future runner wages. The complete future payoff is this amount multiplied by the number of future dinners.

sheets.name: Runner net downside per dinner
sheets.meaning: Net incremental contribution after future runner wages, usually negative. Future wages must not be subtracted a second time.

sheets.name: Other staff commitments
sheets.meaning: Complete recorded outside commitments remain part of every study-and-response operating check.

sheets.name: Explicit probability basis
sheets.meaning: A stated source and exact scope for probability judgments. Evidence interpretation counts do not supply probabilities.

sheets.name: Prior staffing probabilities
sheets.meaning: One explicit probability for each authored situation, summing to one.

sheets.name: Study likelihood assumptions
sheets.meaning: A complete likelihood matrix for both designs, including no usable answer. These judgments remain separate from the actual evidence audit.

sheets.name: Report likelihoods
sheets.meaning: A complete likelihood matrix for both designs, including no usable answer. These judgments remain separate from the actual evidence audit.

sheets.name: Optional actual report and rema
sheets.meaning: Optional received records and remaining operating horizon. Receipt alone never establishes the staffing situation or authorizes a staffing change.

probabilityBasis.source: Fictional teaching judgments: 50/50 prior, audit 70/30, trial 90/10. These are not accuracy estimates inferred from restaurant records.
probabilityBasis.scope: The named runner role, comparable future dinner services, and the declared staffing decision.
